prompt: Repeatedly sum the digits of a non-negative int until a single digit remains. Complete the digitalRoot method in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: This problem nests one loop inside another in a less obvious way: the inner loop sums the digits of the current value using % 10 and / 10, and the outer loop repeats that whole process until the value drops below 10. Resetting the digit sum to 0 at the start of every outer pass is essential -- forgetting it carries old totals forward. The condition n >= 10 is exactly 'n has more than one digit' for non-negative n.
hints: A number is a single digit exactly when it is less than 10, so the outer loop runs while n >= 10.
Inside, sum the digits of n with the usual pattern: sum += n % 10 then divide n by 10, looping while the value is positive.
After the inner loop finishes, assign the digit sum back to n and let the outer loop decide whether another round is needed. Reset sum to 0 each round.
